instruction.name: movgr2frh.w
instruction.description: Move the low 32 bits of rj into the high 32 bits of fd.

latencies.notes: 3 cycles for this direction. The split between the two directions is not observable on this core: every closed chain crosses the boundary both ways, so only the sum shows up (the round trip measures 5.00 cycles and stays additive). The split is fixed by the microarchitecture: an FPR load cannot take the address-bypass path, so `fld.d $f0, $r4, 0; movfr2gr.d $r4, $f0` (6.98 cycles) has to be a 5-cycle load plus a 2-cycle move, and the 5.00-cycle FPR round trip then puts the other direction at 2. The stored experiment is the round trip itself, with the opposite direction subtracted as chain_latency.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: movgr2frh.w $f0, $r4; movgr2frh.w $f1, $r5; movgr2frh.w $f2, $r6; movgr2frh.w $f3, $r7; movgr2frh.w $f4, $r8; movgr2frh.w $f5, $r9; movgr2frh.w $f6, $r10; movgr2frh.w $f7, $r11

throughput.notes: 8 independent instructions take 8.00 cycles. Extra counters per instruction (normalized by 8 lanes): 0xfc=1.00.

notes: High-half GPR->FPR move. Retires as 2 uops; write latency is 2 cycles versus 1 cycle for movgr2fr.d/w. Round trip with movfrh2gr.s is 5 cycles. Throughput is 1 CPI.
